description:
**MakerSpark** is an 8-hour hardware-only hackathon organized by the **IEEE Sensors Council Kerala Chapter**, in collaboration with **Arduino, Maker Village, and Semicon Keralam**. Hosted at the **Indian Institute of Information Technology and Management–Kerala (IIITM-K), Technopark, Thiruvananthapuram**, the event brings together aspiring innovators, engineers, and technology enthusiasts to transform creative ideas into impactful hardware solutions.

Shortlisted participants will be provided with **Arduino UNO Q** boards and will be required to develop Physical AI-based projects **using the board as a mandatory component** during the hackathon.


***TRACKS***
**1. Industry 2.0 – The Future of Automation**
Centred on the future of industries, exploring intelligent automation, industrial transformation, robotics, and the evolution of manufacturing and production systems.

**2. HealthTech – Beyond Boundaries**
Exploring the role of technology in revolutionising healthcare, focusing on medical innovation, healthcare accessibility, patient well-being, and advancements in health technologies.

**3. Utopia – Envisioning a Better World**
Dedicated to technological innovation for a better future, encompassing sustainability, environmental protection, smart living, and solutions to societal challenges.

**4. Odyssey – A Journey to Limitless Possibilities**
Ideas that transcend conventional domains, embracing interdisciplinary innovation, emerging technologies, creative problem-solving, and unexplored possibilities.

**Join our community :**
https://chat.whatsapp.com/LPajlPT39biATzNpKs3tLW

hackathon_faqs.answer:
# MakerSpark – Rules & Regulations

### 1. Eligibility
- The hackathon is open to students.
- Participants must complete the registration process through Devfolio before the deadline.
- Every participant must carry a valid student ID for verification during the event.
- Each participant may be a member of only one team.

### 2. Team Formation
- Teams must consist of 1–4 members.
- Once registrations are closed, changes to team composition will only be permitted under exceptional circumstances and with approval from the organizing committee.

### 3. Code of Conduct
Participants are expected to maintain a respectful, inclusive, and professional environment throughout the event.

- Treat fellow participants, mentors, judges, volunteers, sponsors, and organizers with respect.
- Refrain from harassment, discrimination, intimidation, or disruptive behaviour.
- Follow all venue policies and safety guidelines.
- Foster collaboration and healthy competition.

Violation of the Code of Conduct may result in immediate disqualification and removal from the event.

### 4. Use of AI Tools
The use of AI-assisted tools such as ChatGPT, GitHub Copilot, and similar technologies is permitted for ideation, coding assistance, debugging, documentation, and design support.

However:
- Teams must fully understand every aspect of their solution.
- Judges may question participants regarding any part of the implementation.
- Teams remain solely responsible for the originality, correctness, and ethical use of AI-generated content.

### 5. Intellectual Property
Participants retain ownership of the intellectual property developed during the hackathon.

By participating, teams grant the organizers permission to use project titles, abstracts, screenshots, photographs, videos, and demonstrations for promotional, educational, and documentation purposes.

### 6. Fair Play & Academic Integrity
Participants are expected to uphold the highest standards of academic and professional integrity.

The following actions are strictly prohibited:
- Plagiarism.
- Copying existing projects without substantial original contribution.
- Misrepresentation of work.
- Sharing confidential project code with competing teams.
- Tampering with another team's work.
- Any attempt to manipulate the judging process.

Violations may result in immediate disqualification.

### 7. Equipment and Components
Teams are responsible for bringing the necessary components, tools, and equipment required for developing their hardware solutions, unless otherwise specified by the organizers.

**The Arduino UNO Q board will be provided to all participating teams at the venue and its use is mandatory. All projects must be Physical AI-based and developed using the Arduino UNO Q as a core component.**

Selected sensors available with the organizers will also be provided to participants for use during the hackathon.

Projects involving hazardous materials or unsafe practices may require prior approval from the organizing committee.

### 8. Organizer Rights
The organizing committee reserves the right to:
- Modify the schedule due to unforeseen circumstances.
- Clarify or amend these rules whenever necessary.
- Merge, restructure, or revise event activities if required.
- Disqualify teams violating hackathon policies.
- Resolve disputes, with all decisions being final.

### 9. Acceptance of Rules
By registering for MakerSpark, participants acknowledge that they have read, understood, and agreed to abide by these Rules & Regulations and all decisions made by the organizing committee.
